content.value_statement: Large module sets become hard to maintain when size, documentation, and ratios drift. This skill reviews Logseq module structure and recommends focused refactors.
actual_capabilities: Counts Logseq classes and properties in source module files.
Calculates per-module and overall health scores from documented rules.
Flags bloated, very small, empty, and undocumented modules.
Suggests split strategies for mixed modules such as misc.
Supports quick checks, deep dives, reorganization plans, and trend reviews.
Includes Bash and PowerShell helper scripts for local health checks.
limitations: Designed for the Logseq Template Graph module layout, not arbitrary project architectures.
Scores are heuristic and should be reviewed before major refactors.
Dependency and trend analysis may require local file access and git history.
The helper scripts only report health; they do not perform migrations.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Module Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find oversized, small, or undocumented modules before planning maintenance work.

use_cases.title: Plan Architecture Refactors
use_cases.description: Group mixed classes into focused modules and estimate the impact of a split.

use_cases.title: Review New Contributions
use_cases.description: Check that proposed module changes preserve balance, clarity, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Health Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a current project snapshot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a quick health check for the Logseq Template Graph modules and summarize the top three issues.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a module that may be too broad.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the misc module in detail. Group classes by domain and suggest a split plan with estimated effort.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Health Over Time
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review using recent repository history.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare module health with recent git history. Highlight modules that grew, shrank, or became less cohesive.

prompt_templates.title: Create Refactoring Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across the full module architecture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactoring roadmap for improving overall module health from the current score to a better target.

output_examples.output: A health report with an overall score, module table, top issues, and priority recommendation.

output_examples.input: Analyze the misc module in detail.
output_examples.output: A domain grouping summary, proposed new modules, estimated effort, and expected score improvement.
A trend summary that compares module counts, recent changes, growing modules, and architecture risks.

best_practices: Run a quick check before large ontology or schema changes.
Review split recommendations against domain knowledge before moving classes.
Use scores as a prioritization guide, then validate builds after refactoring.
anti_patterns: Treating the health score as the only architecture decision.
Splitting modules before checking dependencies and shared properties.
Running helper scripts from an unrelated project root.

faq.question: What project layout does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects the Logseq Template Graph source module layout with classes, properties, and README files.

faq.question: Does the skill change files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports health, explains risks, and recommends refactors unless the user requests edits.

faq.question: What files does it inspect?
faq.answer: It reads module class files, property files, README files, and optionally git history for trends.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How are health scores calculated?
faq.answer: Scores use module size, documentation, completeness, class-to-property ratios, and organization quality.

faq.question: Are the shell scripts required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional local helpers for quick checks and do not perform migrations.
